canonical_name: Erdos-Stone finite simple-graph extremal theorem family
literal_source_claim: A fundamental theorem of extremal graph theory.
candidate_claims_not_credited_as_stateme: The complement-form theorem on page 1088 of Erdos and Stone (1946): edge count above (1/2 - 1/(2(r-1)) + epsilon) times n squared forces a growing complete r-partite subgraph.
For each fixed finite simple graph H with chromatic number at least two, extremalNumber n H is asymptotic to (1 - 1/(chromaticNumber H - 1)) times n squared over two.
Equivalently, under resolved finiteness and nondegeneracy hypotheses, turanDensity H equals 1 - 1/(chromaticNumber H - 1).
domain_and_universes: Candidate scope: finite simple graphs, natural vertex counts and part parameters, real edge-density tolerances, graph containment, and finite chromatic number. Exact universes, finiteness instances, coercions, and nondegeneracy conditions remain open.
conclusion: Open: choose and source-review the original complete-equipartite containment statement, the modern fixed-forbidden-graph asymptotic density formula, or a checked equivalence package before freezing one exact conclusion.
degenerate_cases_to_resolve: empty forbidden graph and empty vertex type
edgeless forbidden graph and chromatic number zero or one
bipartite forbidden graph with zero Turan density
infinite or top-valued chromatic number encodings
r equal to zero or one and complete-equipartite part size zero
epsilon outside the original zero-to-one range
excluded_substitutions: a minimum-degree strengthening as the unannounced canonical root
hypergraph, directed, weighted, infinite-graph, graphon, or probabilistic variants
a desired density equality or complete-equipartite copy assumed as an input
an unpinned mathlib commit or catalog verified label as proof evidence

neighbor_target_boundaries.boundary: Simonovits stability is a distinct stronger structural target.
